title: Minimax Logarithmic Cost of Limited Probability Changes for Gaussian A2IPW Designs
banked_reason: D0.5 decision panel found kernel substitution; cold review rated the sound result incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The proposal's unrestricted adaptive-A2IPW global minimax limit M_T/log T to 24 with a data-only attaining rule has been replaced by a fixed-change-budget bracket (16 log T below and polynomial achievability above), so the advertised exact second-order result is not delivered.

The requested sharp global result, M_T/log T tending to 24, is not proved; the note instead studies a newly imposed fixed-change budget and obtains only a 16 log T lower bound versus a T^{1/(K+1)} upper bound.
proof_attempt_summary: The first angle proposed an unrestricted Gaussian A2IPW minimax logarithmic constant of 24 but exhausted its proposal revision budget after source-attribution defects. The second angle proved an exact conditional-variance identity and sound fixed-update lower and upper results, including a closed-form recursive announced-calendar upper coefficient; adaptive stopping invalidated the proposed exact fixed-update converse. A stopped-experiment converse for all continuously monitored policies is still needed to determine the positive-budget minimax normalization and constant, and the original unrestricted constant remains unproved.
tldr: With at most \(K\) predictable probability changes, the exact A2IPW loss retains its rank-one augmentation square and cross-arm product. A posterior-state Bellman game valid for continuously monitored changes gives \(M_{T,K}\ge(16-o(1))\log T\). For every fixed positive \(K\), a data-only rule recursively announces each next endpoint from empirical scales and has the explicit upper coefficient \(\mathcal U_K=8K[K(8-\{4(9/2)^{K-1}\}^{1/K})]^{-1/(K+1)}\). It satisfies \(\mathcal U_1=\mathcal C_1=4\) and \(\mathcal U_K<\mathcal C_K\) for every \(K\ge2\), where \(\mathcal C_K\) is only a deterministic-calendar upper comparator. The zero-change limit is exact, but the true continuously monitored fixed- and growing-budget minimax constants remain open.
gap: Published fully sequential results include ClipSMT regret for an adaptive Horvitz--Thompson allocation criterion, OPTrack regret for A2IPW, and anytime design-based Neyman regret; published multistage Neyman design instead studies a difference-in-means proxy criterion. None identifies the minimax precision price of a finite probability-update budget for the Gaussian superpopulation A2IPW score.
fill: The project derives the exact loss with its cross-arm term, reduces the fixed-update problem to a sharp schedule-information game, proves that predictable random update times do not improve its value, and supplies an empirical-scale allocation with empirical-mean augmentation that attains the resulting calendar.
